key_insight: Extending characteristic mapping to dissipative equations preserves its fine-scale resolution strategy while enabling simulations that include viscosity.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support multiscale Navier–Stokes simulations across Reynolds-number regimes, though broad performance gains remain to be established.
method: Lift scalar evolution into a path of diffeomorphisms, interpreted through optimal transport.
Represent the flow map as a composition of spatial interpolants and evolve it with semi-Lagrangian characteristic mapping.
Use semidirect-product time stepping with an explicit exponential integrator for the log-Jacobian.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-order accuracy and tests on canonical nonlinear dissipative equations, but provides no quantitative errors or runtime comparisons.
watch_item: Robustness and computational cost for high-Reynolds-number turbulent flows require further validation.
paper_title: A characteristic mapping method for dissipative evolution equations
